public_rationale: Reuters reported on January 30, 2026 that Starlink's January 15 policy update permitted AI training unless users opted out, but the report does not establish what notices affected users received [e1]. Vercel's March 17, 2026 announcement described an opt-out deadline of March 31 [e2]. A March 8, 2025 account described Pinterest's planned default inclusion under a policy effective April 30, with a settings opt-out and advance notice [e3]. These records do not establish two companies introducing the complete practice of default training inclusion with obscure disclosure, or a decisive development ruling out further adoption [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Original Starlink user notices and interface records are missing.
A public announcement alone does not establish the visibility of notice to every affected user.
Pinterest's advance notice is described in a secondary account.
Policy permission does not prove that training occurred.
The forecast has no deadline, and the reviewed examples do not establish what happened across all companies.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: More companies will follow an opt-out playbook to collect training data, hiding it in obscure settings and Terms of Service.

statement.excerpt: Every big tech company is desperate for training data, and we can expect more companies following the same sly opt-out playbook, hiding what is going in obscure settings and Terms of Service nobody reads.
statement.document_title: PSA: Microsoft may be training on your private data without your knowledge

from_speaker: following the same sly opt-out playbook
hiding what is going in obscure settings and Terms of Service nobody reads
our_interpretation: The graded forecast concerns additional companies adopting the practice after November 26, 2024.
More companies requires multiple additional companies; two is a minimum, not a claim about widespread prevalence.
Hiding is assessed through disclosure and interface design, not an inferred motive. Default training alone is insufficient.
Nobody reads is rhetorical emphasis on poor visibility, not a literal claim that no person reads terms.
The prefatory assertion about every company's desperation is not part of this extracted forecast.
criteria.support_condition: At least two additional companies introduce default inclusion of user data in AI training after the post, with evidence that notice and opt-outs were confined to obscure settings or terms rather than clearly presented to affected users.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive development rules out the predicted additional adoption. Failure to find examples by an arbitrary date cannot contradict an undated forecast.

evidence.locator: Paragraph following the description of data Starlink collects
evidence.explanation: Reuters documents a new opt-out training permission and unclear data scope. It does not establish whether affected users received prominent notices or whether training had actually begun.

evidence.locator: FAQ: When do I have to opt-out before my data is shared?
evidence.explanation: The announcement specifies default inclusion for Hobby and trial accounts, with paid Pro and Enterprise excluded by default. Its advance announcement prevents treating the policy alone as proof of concealed disclosure.
The account describes default inclusion and a settings opt-out, but also advance notice. This makes Pinterest an uncertain example of the complete concealed-disclosure forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Dated records establishing that at least two additional companies introduced default AI-training inclusion after November 26, 2024, with notices and opt-outs confined to obscure settings or terms. Each case needs the introduction date, data scope, default, opt-out path, and user notices. A decisive development ruling out further qualifying adoption could instead contradict the forecast.
